sections.h2: Three common fences in High Springs
body: Picket fences near Historic Downtown. These are usually painted to match or complement the trim on a craftsman house. They need the same care as the house trim: scrape loose paint, spot-prime, and use a flexible 100% acrylic topcoat.

Privacy fences in Bridlewood and Bailey Estates. These are mostly pressure-treated boards that have turned gray. A penetrating stain soaks in and won't peel, which is why we usually recommend it for fence staining in High Springs, FL.

Board fencing along the Poe Springs corridor. These long runs see hours of sun on one side and shade on the other. Washing, a few replacement boards, and stain make up most of the work. Footage drives the schedule, so we measure every run during the walkthrough.

In this climate, the shaded side of a fence grows mildew and algae the same way a north wall does. If you stain or paint over live growth, the finish will fail early. We treat it at the root, rinse, and let the boards dry before applying anything. The sunny side has the opposite problem: gray, fuzzy fibers from UV damage. Our guide to sun-damaged wood fences covers how that surface is restored.

bullets: Soft wash to remove mildew and gray fibers
Light sanding on fuzzy or splintered boards
Replace broken pickets, boards, and rails, each listed on the estimate first
Spot-prime bare wood on painted fences
Spray and back-brush stain into the gaps and end grain

body: A fence looks best when it relates to the house, whether that's painted pickets that match the trim or stained boards that match the deck. If both are on your list, schedule them together with deck staining in High Springs so one product and color carry through. For help choosing colors, see the High Springs color consult. Our general Florida fence staining page goes deeper on products, and the High Springs page lists every service in town.

faqs.q: Should my picket fence be painted or stained?
faqs.a: If it's already painted, or it's meant to match painted trim on the house, paint it. For raw or previously stained wood, a penetrating stain is usually easier to maintain because it doesn't peel.

faqs.q: Do you treat mildew on fences?
faqs.a: Yes. The fence is soft washed with a cleaning solution that treats the growth at the root, then rinsed and allowed to dry before any stain or paint goes on.

faqs.q: Can you do just my side of a shared fence?
faqs.a: Yes. If you only have access to one side or your neighbor prefers to leave theirs as is, the estimate will state which faces of the fence are included.

faqs.q: Can you handle a long fence on acreage?
faqs.a: Yes. Long runs are measured during the walkthrough, and the written estimate includes the footage, repairs, product, and a schedule that allows for dry time.
